text:
anya (PM): quick sync — I'm kicking off recruitment for the design partner / beta cohort for the new routing+cache controls. need to align on screening, incentives, and what we actually measure.

sam (Eng): sounds good. timeline? i can support onboarding + short runbook for folks.

anya (PM): target kickoff outreach next week. goal: 6–8 partners for a 6 week beta. 2 must be enterprise, 2 mid-market, 2 startups.

lee (Design): suggested success criteria from design side: 1) integration <2 days for engineers, 2) observed decrease in 95p latency for routed requests when cache hits >=20%, 3) qualitative satisfaction >=4/5 in end-of-beta survey.

maria (Customer Success): will help screen candidates. ask prioritization: willingness to share perf metrics, dedicated contact for weekly check-ins, NDA signed. incentive: $10k credit + prioritized roadmap input. ok?

sam (Eng): agree. also need to check data sharing — we should clarify what logs we need vs what stays on-prem for private deployments. include minimal telemetry list: model, route, latency_ms, token_count, error_code.

anya (PM): good call. draft outreach message below — please edit.

anya (PM): ```
Hi <Name>,
We'd love to invite <Company> to join Redwood's Design Partner beta for our Routing & Cache Controls.
What you'll get: dedicated onboarding, $10k usage credit, weekly ops support, and direct influence on product decisions.
What we ask: 6–8 weeks of collaborative testing, basic telemetry (latency, errors, token counts), and 30–60m weekly syncs.
If interested, reply with a contact and preferred start window.
Thanks!
-Anya
```

lee (Design): tweak: add an explicit privacy line: "We only request aggregated telemetry; raw user data never leaves your VPC unless you opt in."

maria (Customer Success): screening checklist I'm going to use: 1) tech contact + PM, 2) SLA/uptime needs, 3) typical QPS and seq_len distribution, 4) compliance constraints (PII/PCI/HIPAA), 5) willingness to sign NDA. I'll send to our customer shortlist today.

sam (Eng): onboarding runbook items: pre-check list (network/VPC peering if private, API keys, model versions), sample workload script, canary traffic plan, rollback steps. i'll draft this and link in doc.

ops-bot: new doc created: /product/dp-beta/onboarding-runbook v0.1

anya (PM): feedback loop cadence proposal: weekly 30–60m sync + asynchronous channel in slack private DP workspace. do quick feedback surveys at week 2, week 4, and post-beta. collect both quantitative (NPS, satisfaction, latency percentiles) and qualitative (open text).

lee (Design): sample survey Qs: 1) Did the controls reduce manual tuning time? (yes/no + mins saved) 2) Was performance change noticeable? (none/small/medium/large) 3) Rate overall UX 1–5. 4) Open: what broke or surprised you?

maria (Customer Success): measurement plan: we want to capture baseline week before any changes, then weekly snapshots. metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token cost per 1k, cache hit ratio, incidents. baseline will be part of screening.

anya (PM): launch criteria to graduate from beta: 
- 95% of partners report integration completed within agreed timeframe
- p95 latency improvement >=10% on at least 4 partners (or no material regressions)
- no P0 production incidents attributable to new routing control during last 2 weeks
- documented runbook and one successful self-serve integration by a partner
- at least 75% positive qualitative feedback (>=4/5)

sam (Eng): agree. add: performance regression alerting and auto-fallback must be in place.

lee (Design): also ensure we have before/after screenshots of console flows + a short walkthrough video for future customers.

maria (Customer Success): will prepare consent + NDA template. what about legal signoff for enterprise partners? anya, can you loop in legal if any enterprise wants non-standard terms?

anya (PM): yes — will loop in legal only if they ask for exceptions. otherwise we'll use standard DP contract.

sam (Eng): capacity-wise, for 8 partners we should reserve a dedicated burst pool for one-month windows. ops, can we provision?

ops-bot: requested: infra ticket #INF-4331 created to reserve burst pool for DP cohort. assignee: infra-oncall.

maria (Customer Success): outreach plan: send personalized note to 12 candidates, expect 50% opt-in -> aim to convert 6. i'll prioritize active users with recent higher QPS.

anya (PM): risks: 1) partners drop mid-beta — mitigation: staggered starts, continuous recruiting 2) we collect incomplete telemetry — mitigation: pre-flight checklist + sample script 3) feature not mature — mitigation: clear expectations + quick rollback.

lee (Design): can we offer a 2-week pilot for hesitant parties? smaller scope: only routing decisions, no cache.

anya (PM): yes — we can offer pilot. offer timeline and commit level in outreach.

maria (Customer Success): i'll send the outreach today and update this thread with responses.

anya (PM): perfect. next steps: sam drafts runbook by EOD Fri, lee finalizes survey + UX assets, maria starts outreach. we'll reconvene Mon for candidate shortlist. thanks team :rocket:
